the 1950s Headlam led experimental research into combat tactics and air-to-air missile systems and established the Armament Research & Development Unit to work on an early generation of air-to-air missiles, such as Blue Steel. He was appointed Commander of No. 214 Group in August 1956, and was knighted as a Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath in the 1957 New Year Honours. After that Headlam was appointed Chief of Staff at RAF Bomber Command in 1959 and became Commander of No. 4 (Bomber) Group in 1960. His last appointments were as Air Officer Commanding No. 21 (Bomber) Group in 1962 and as Air Member for Personnel at the Air Ministry in 1964. Headlam retired on 28 August 1967 and died at Abingdon, Oxfordshire, on 19 August 1995.

## Monuments

The only monument directly related to Chak Tok Ich 'aak I is his sarcophagus. The tomb was the second tomb found in the North Acropolis, and one of the four richest. It was a small and standard pit, with four steps. Stela 34 may mention this king, but only the traces of the name remain.
